topic.source_contract: Railway proximity, asset protection, level-crossing consultation, drainage, property agreements and delivery evidence

facts.consultation: traffic increases or character changes at level crossings trigger consultation
facts.guard: consultation is not safety acceptance or closure order

facts.aspro: ASPRO supports work planned on or near the railway
facts.guard: ASPRO contact is not an asset-protection agreement or approval

facts.agreements: property agreement and basic asset-protection agreement may both be required
facts.guard: one agreement does not replace the other

facts.documents: development-services and asset-protection guidance for third parties
facts.guard: guidance is not a signed project agreement

facts.drainage: development near railway can increase runoff to tracks
facts.guard: planning drainage statement is not Network Rail technical acceptance

scope_guards: Railway proximity is not treated as permission to access or build on railway land.
Planning permission is not treated as Network Rail asset-protection acceptance.
ASPRO engagement is not treated as a signed BAPA, APA or development-services agreement.
A level-crossing consultation is not treated as safety approval or capacity confirmation.
A property agreement is not treated as technical approval.
Drainage design is not treated as accepted until railway impacts and discharge routes are agreed.
Possession or isolation concepts are not treated as booked railway access.
No score or promotion is written without exact railway boundary, agreements, design acceptance, possessions, approvals and completion evidence.
